source.subject: test: reject persistent packed NVFP4 Down P0

environment.claim_scope: one fixed-clock stop-loss process for one exact Down M256 mechanism probe

shape.weight_format: NVFP4 E2M1 packed with FP8 block-16 scales

experiment.baseline: selected whole-chunk N-major M256 kernel, grid 160
experiment.candidate: fixed grid 16, static stride over 160 M64xN128 logical tasks

sidecars.weights: projection-local NK64 reorder, byte count equal to the canonical Down packed weights
sidecars.scales: projection-local NK256 reorder, byte count equal to the canonical Down scales

implemented: established synchronous K64 shared-memory WMMA arithmetic
not_implemented_or_claimed: register-resident E2M1 decode plus direct MMA
B arithmetic reuse across more than one M64 task

focused_rejection_log.terminal_summary: 19 NVFP4 down persistent packed P0 assertion(s) failed

decision.rejected_mechanism: fixed 16-CTA persistence plus byte-reordered sidecars without intra-CTA B arithmetic reuse or a real asynchronous pipeline
decision.reason: Reducing the selected 160-CTA grid to 16 CTAs lowers realized parallelism from up to three resident CTAs/SM to one launched CTA/SM, while each logical M64 task still repeats the same B decode and WMMA work. The approximately 0.511x result is the expected near-2x regression.
decision.next_valid_probe: A future persistent design must make each CTA reuse one B tile across at least M128/M256 work and/or implement the actual multistage packed-B/register-decode pipeline before reducing the grid. Static persistence alone is closed.

limitations: This deliberately incomplete P0 isolates and rejects a scheduling mechanism; it does not reject a true Marlin-style dataflow.
Sidecar preparation and its temporary memory cost are excluded from timing.
The strong stop-loss rejection uses one process rather than three because every one of 18 mirrored rounds regresses by about 49%.
Production code and default dispatch are unchanged.
